title: All-at-once refinement of a pointed inverse system
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $(J,\geq,V_j,g_{jj'})$ be a directed inverse system of objects of $\mathcal C$: $J$ is a nonempty directed poset, each $j\geq j'$ has a transition $g_{jj'}:V_j\to V_{j'}$, and the transitions satisfy $g_{jj}=\mathrm{id}$ and $g_{j'j''}g_{jj'}=g_{jj''}$. Put $u'(W)=\varinjlim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V_j,W)$ and $\mathcal F_{p'}=\varinjlim_{j\in J}\mathcal F(V_j)$ for a sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$. If $s\ne s'$ in $\mathcal F_{p'}$, then there is a directed inverse system $(I,\geq,U_i,f_{ii'})$ refining the given one (so $J\subset I$, $U_j=V_j$ and $f_{jj'}=g_{jj'}$ on $J$) such that the images of $s,s'$ in $\varinjlim_i\mathcal F(U_i)$ remain distinct and, for every finite covering $\{W_k\to W\}$ of $\mathcal C$ and every $f\in u'(W)$, the image of $f$ in $u(W)=\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(U_i,W)$ lies in the image of $u(W_k)\to u(W)$ for some $k$, i.e. it is represented by the composite of some $U_i\to W_k$ with $W_k\to W$.

source.place: Tag 00YP (Lemma lemma-refine-all-at-once), in the proof of Tag 00YQ (Proposition proposition-criterion-points).

proof.text: Let $E$ be the set of pairs $(\{W_k\to W\},f\in u'(W))$ consisting of a finite covering and an element of the original functor $u'$. It is a set because the site has sets of objects, morphisms, and covering families, and each $u'(W)$ is a set-valued filtered colimit. We construct, for each initial segment of a well-ordering of $E$, a refinement system together with the invariant that the images of $s,s'$ are distinct and all pairs in that initial segment have the required lifting property. The empty initial segment is realized by the original system $(J,V_j,g_{jj'})$.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof: define E and the class S of partial refinements

proof.text: At a successor stage for $e=(\{W_k\to W\},f)$, apply [lem-trf-point-system-refine] to the current system and the still-distinct images of $s,s'$. It produces a refinement preserving distinctness and making the image of $f$ factor through one member $W_k$. At a limit stage, take the union of the previously constructed nested index systems, with the induced order, objects, and transition maps. The union is again a directed inverse system: two indices already occur together in one earlier system, which supplies an upper bound, and the transition maps agree because the systems form a chain of refinements.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof: successor step by Lemma 00YO and union at limit stages

proof.text: The distinctness invariant survives a limit union. If the two classes became equal in the union colimit, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] would give a common later index witnessing equality. That index and the two representatives occur in some member of the nested chain, where distinctness was maintained, a contradiction. Thus every stage of the recursion has a valid invariant and the transfinite recursion is defined for the whole well-order of $E$.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof: chain-union condition (2) and directed-colimit equality criterion

proof.text: Take the union over all $e\in E$. It is a refinement of the original system and its two images of $s,s'$ remain distinct by the preceding argument. For any pair $(\{W_k\to W\},f)\in E$, the stage at which that pair was processed supplied a representative through some $W_k$; passing to the final union preserves that factorization. Therefore every finite covering and every $f\in u'(W)$ has the required lift in the final $u(W)$, proving the statement.

source.place: Tag 00YP, proof: final union over the well-order E
